_about: Every text CRANE-LLM shows to users, for both the JupyterLab extension and the %%crane_llm magic. Words in {braces} are filled in at runtime; keep them. After editing: run reload_crane_llm() in a notebook for the magic and the backend, and `jlpm build` in crane_llm/nb_extension, then refresh the browser, for JupyterLab.

guard.label: Check cells before they run
guard.hint_on: The built-in checker checks each cell first, and a cell it finds will crash is not run. The LLM is never used for this.
guard.hint_off: Cells run without being checked. When on, only the built-in checker is used, never the LLM.
guard.verdict_label: not run, this cell would crash
guard.footer: Nothing in this cell was executed. To run it anyway, add the line `# crane: run` to it. To stop checking cells before they run, switch off "Check cells before they run" in JupyterLab, or run `%crane_llm guard off`.
guard.error: CRANE-LLM did not run this cell. {reasoning}
guard.magic_on: CRANE-LLM checks every cell before it runs, until the kernel restarts. A cell the built-in checker finds will crash is not run.
guard.magic_off: CRANE-LLM does not check cells before they run.
guard.magic_usage: Usage: %crane_llm guard on | %crane_llm guard off. To check a single cell, put %%crane_llm on its first line instead.
guard.unavailable_title: Cells in this notebook are not being checked

chatgpt.warning: Experimental. "Continue with ChatGPT" lets CRANE-LLM use your ChatGPT plan instead of an API key, through OpenAI's sign-in for open-source tools. Requests count against your plan's usage limits (on Plus, the five-hour limit is shared with every other app using it; see https://chatgpt.com/settings/usage). CRANE-LLM gets no access to your ChatGPT conversations. You can disconnect it at any time in ChatGPT's settings.
chatgpt.already_signed_in: Already signed in as {account}. Sign in again?
chatgpt.browser_instructions:
Continue with ChatGPT: a browser tab should open. If it does not, open this link on this computer:

  {url}

The first time, ChatGPT asks you to approve CRANE-LLM for your account.
Waiting for you to finish (up to 10 minutes; interrupt the kernel to cancel)...
chatgpt.browser_done: CRANE-LLM is signed in. You can close this tab and return to the notebook.
chatgpt.port_busy: Port {port} on 127.0.0.1 is in use, and the first ChatGPT sign-in has to receive the browser's answer there. Close what uses it (often another tool's sign-in) and run crane_llm.setup("chatgpt") again.
chatgpt.login_timeout: The ChatGPT sign-in was not completed in time. Run crane_llm.setup("chatgpt") again. If the browser could not reach http://127.0.0.1, the kernel runs on another machine: see the user guide for an SSH tunnel.
chatgpt.bad_callback: The ChatGPT sign-in returned an answer that does not match this attempt, so it was ignored. Run crane_llm.setup("chatgpt") again.
chatgpt.access_denied: The ChatGPT sign-in was cancelled in the browser. Nothing was saved.
chatgpt.exchange_failed: The ChatGPT sign-in could not be completed (HTTP {status}). Run crane_llm.setup("chatgpt") again.
chatgpt.bad_id_token: The ChatGPT sign-in returned an identity token that failed its checks ({problems}), so it was not used.
chatgpt.plan_not_granted: You signed in, but using your ChatGPT plan was not allowed for CRANE-LLM, so the LLM cannot be asked this way. Run crane_llm.setup("chatgpt") again and allow plan usage, or choose an API key with crane_llm.setup().
chatgpt.refresh_failed: Could not renew the ChatGPT session (HTTP {status}). Try again in a minute; you stay signed in.

errors.missing_key_kaggle:
No API key found, so the LLM was not asked. On Kaggle, store it as a secret:

  1. In the notebook editor, open Add-ons > Secrets.
  2. Add a secret with the label CRANE_LLM_API_KEY and your key as the value.
  3. Tick the checkbox next to it, so this notebook may read it.

Then run the %%crane_llm cell again; no restart is needed. Keep the key
out of the notebook itself, which others can read once it is shared.

To use the built-in checker only, which needs no key, write %%crane_llm --no-llm instead.
errors.missing_key_colab:
No API key found, so the LLM was not asked. On Colab, store it as a secret:

  1. Click the key icon in the left sidebar (Secrets).
  2. Add a secret named CRANE_LLM_API_KEY with your key as the value.
  3. Switch on 'Notebook access' for it.

Then run the %%crane_llm cell again; no restart is needed.

To use the built-in checker only, which needs no key, write %%crane_llm --no-llm instead.
errors.missing_key:
No API key found, so the LLM was not asked. Set up a model, then retry.

In any notebook cell, saved to {path} for future sessions:
         import crane_llm
         crane_llm.setup()

It lists the supported providers (OpenAI, a ChatGPT subscription, OpenRouter,
Gemini, Groq, a local Ollama server, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and
asks only what the one you pick needs.

A key can also come from an environment variable, or a .env file in the
directory you started Jupyter from:
         CRANE_LLM_API_KEY=sk-...

To use the built-in checker only, which needs no key, switch off "Use the LLM" in
JupyterLab, or write %%crane_llm --no-llm with the cell magic.
errors.key_rejected:
The API key was rejected by {endpoint}: {reason}

Check that the key is correct and belongs to that provider. To enter it again,
or to pick another provider, run in any cell:
         import crane_llm
         crane_llm.setup()

To use the built-in checker only, which needs no key, switch off "Use the LLM" in
JupyterLab, or write %%crane_llm --no-llm with the cell magic.
errors.chatgpt_not_logged_in:
CRANE-LLM is set up to use your ChatGPT plan, but you are not signed in, so the LLM was not asked. Sign in from any notebook cell:
         import crane_llm
         crane_llm.setup("chatgpt")

To use the built-in checker only, which needs no key, switch off "Use the LLM" in
JupyterLab, or write %%crane_llm --no-llm with the cell magic.
errors.chatgpt_session_expired:
The ChatGPT session has expired, or CRANE-LLM was disconnected in ChatGPT's settings, so the LLM was not asked. Sign in again from any notebook cell:
         import crane_llm
         crane_llm.setup("chatgpt", relogin=True)

To use the built-in checker only, which needs no key, switch off "Use the LLM" in
JupyterLab, or write %%crane_llm --no-llm with the cell magic.
errors.chatgpt_hosted_unsupported: Continue with ChatGPT needs the browser and the kernel on the same computer, which Kaggle and Colab do not offer. Use an API key there, stored as a notebook secret named CRANE_LLM_API_KEY.
errors.chatgpt_invalid_client: ChatGPT no longer recognises this CRANE-LLM registration. Delete chatgpt_auth.json in ~/.crane_llm and run crane_llm.setup("chatgpt") to register again.
errors.chatgpt_usage_limit:
Your ChatGPT plan's usage limit for apps like CRANE-LLM has been reached, so the LLM could not answer. Check https://chatgpt.com/settings/usage, wait and try again, or switch to an API key with crane_llm.setup().

To use the built-in checker only, which needs no key, switch off "Use the LLM" in
JupyterLab, or write %%crane_llm --no-llm with the cell magic.
errors.chatgpt_unavailable:
ChatGPT plan usage is temporarily unavailable. Try again in a few minutes.

To use the built-in checker only, which needs no key, switch off "Use the LLM" in
JupyterLab, or write %%crane_llm --no-llm with the cell magic.
errors.chatgpt_not_eligible:
Your ChatGPT account or workspace cannot use its plan in other apps, so the LLM was not asked. Use an API key instead: crane_llm.setup().

To use the built-in checker only, which needs no key, switch off "Use the LLM" in
JupyterLab, or write %%crane_llm --no-llm with the cell magic.
